resolutions.researcher_notes: Searched for a source specifically stating the $1.22B (recorded) cost of Rover Pipeline's Phase 2 segment. Found only whole-project cost figures, never phase-split: (1) FERC Federal Register notice of the original Feb 2015 application (govinfo.gov FR-2015-03-16, docket CP15-93 et al.) states Rover's estimated total project cost as '$4.22 billion' with no phase breakdown; (2) Pipeline & Gas Journal's Oct 2018 'Ongoing Projects' compilation (PN1018-Ongoing-Projects.pdf) lists Rover Pipeline at 'Cost: $4.2 billion' for the full 713-mile project, again undifferentiated by phase; (3) dailyenergyinsider.com and ogj.com FERC-approval articles (May 2018, Nov 2018) on Phase 2 facilities/laterals discuss capacity and mileage but state no dollar figures at all; (4) Energy Transfer's 8-K Q4-2016 earnings release (SEC EDGAR 0001012569-17-000018) reports capex jointly for the Bakken/Rover/Bayou Bridge projects combined, not broken out by pipeline or phase; (5) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects data page and archive index carry only current/recent projects, nothing for a 2017-2018-vintage completed project like Rover. SEC EDGAR full-text search ('Rover' + 'Phase II' + 'billion') surfaced no ET/ETP/ETO filing that isolates a Phase 2 dollar cost either. Web search-engine queries (Bing, DuckDuckGo) for a Rover Phase 2-specific cost figure returned no on-topic hits (DuckDuckGo blocked automated queries; Bing's results were dominated by the unrelated Rover.com pet-sitting brand). No source naming a Phase-2-specific cost of ~$1.22B (or any other figure) was found; leaving UNRESOLVED rather than fabricating a URL or misapplying the whole-project figure to a segment.

verifications.note: Energy Transfer LP FY2019 10-K: investments table lists 'Rover Pipeline 32.6%' as ET's ownership interest (matches recorded Owner1=Energy Transfer 32.57% within rounding); same filing's '2017 Transactions' note explains the Rover Contribution Agreement -- Rover Holdco owns 65% of Rover and is split 50.1% ETO / 49.9% Blackstone, i.e. Blackstone's effective share = 0.65 x 49.9% = 32.44% (matches recorded Owner2=Blackstone 32.44% almost exactly), with the remaining 35% of Rover held outside Holdco -- consistent with the filing's separate related-party disclosures of 'Traverse Rover LLC' (matches recorded Owner3=Traverse 35.00%).

Reuters wire story (via BOE Report), April 29 2026: 'Ares said funds ... would buy 32.4% of Rover' from Blackstone; 'Among the assets owned by Traverse is a 35% stake in Rover'; 'Energy Transfer operates and owns the rest of Rover' -- directly corroborates Blackstone/Ares at 32.4% (recorded 32.44%), Traverse at 35% (recorded 35.00% exactly), and Energy Transfer holding the remainder (recorded 32.57%).

Blackstone's own press release, April 29 2026: 'funds led by its Infrastructure Opportunities strategy ... have acquired a 32.4% stake in the Rover Pipeline ... from funds managed by Blackstone Energy Transition Partners'; 'The asset is operated by an affiliate of Energy Transfer LP' -- corroborates the Blackstone 32.44% figure and Energy Transfer's operating/ownership role.

resolutions.researcher_notes: All three current owners and their percentages corroborate within rounding: Energy Transfer 32.57% (recorded) vs 32.6% (Energy Transfer's own FY2019 10-K, SEC EDGAR); Blackstone 32.44% (recorded) vs 32.4% (Reuters/BOE Report, Pipeline & Gas Journal, and Blackstone's own press release all agree, and is independently derivable from the 10-K's Rover Holdco math: 65% Holdco x 49.9% Blackstone share = 32.44%); Traverse 35.00% (recorded) vs 35% (Reuters/BOE Report explicitly: 'Among the assets owned by Traverse is a 35% stake in Rover', consistent with the 10-K's disclosure of 'Traverse Rover LLC' as a related party and the 65%/35% Holdco/non-Holdco split). Three independent sources (an SEC filing by the operator, a Reuters wire story, and Blackstone's own press release) all agree with the recorded values -- discrepancies are rounding only (32.6 vs 32.57; 32.4 vs 32.44), immaterial. Note: this is the pre-2026-transaction / at-transaction ownership; 'Blackstone' is being replaced by Ares Management as the 32.4% holder per the same April 2026 sources, but the sheet's Owner2 value as recorded ('Blackstone') matches the ownership as of the transaction announcement and the historical structure since 2017, so no value change is proposed here -- flagging for the orchestrator that Owner2 may need updating to 'Ares Management' in a future pass once the sale closes, per the boereport/pgjonline/blackstone.com press coverage already on this row for other columns.
